params.name: Cluster Count
params.tooltip:
How many separate groups of towns to form.

Towns are generated normally and then rearranged into these groups.

params.name: Cluster Sizes
params.tooltip:
How much the clusters differ in size.

Equal gives every cluster the same number of towns. The others let one conurbation dominate, with the rest trailing off - Lopsided most sharply. The exact shape is drawn per map, so the same setting looks different on a different seed.

params.name: Towns Left In Place
params.tooltip:
What share of the generated towns keep the position the map generator gave them.

The rest are moved next to a cluster. The total number of towns never changes, so there is no need to adjust the game's Town Density.

params.name: Isolated Towns
params.tooltip:
What share of the moved towns stay out in the country instead of joining a cluster.

Isolated towns are scaled down, so they read as outlying hamlets.

params.name: Town Spacing
params.tooltip:
How close together towns in a cluster may stand.

600 m is the original behaviour and the densest the game has been seen to accept. Clusters settle very near whatever this is set to, so the looser settings spread a cluster out into a group of towns rather than one mass. Even 1300 m is about twice as dense as the map generator's own spacing.

Loosening this needs more buildable ground, so watch for towns that cannot be placed on a cramped or mountainous map.

params.name: Debug: Map Snapshot
params.tooltip:
FOR MOD DEVELOPERS. Leave this Off for normal play - it changes nothing about how the mod clusters, it only writes data out.

What it does: records the generated map - every town, and the terrain on a 32 m grid - into the game log, so the clustering can be tried out offline instead of generating a map for every experiment.

Snapshot Only also skips the clustering, leaving towns exactly where the generator put them, so the run is over in seconds. Start a new game on the seed you want, wait for 'snapshot complete' in the log, and quit - nothing has been changed.

Then run tools\snapshot.ps1 to recover it and tools\studio.ps1 to explore every setting against that map. See tools\preview\README.md.
